popup.title: The Wandering Wemic
popup.description: Rooms could be had at the Wandering Wemic at a rate of 10 gp per night and included stabling, a valet service used for cleaning or repairing gear, and one bottle of wine per person per evening.

popup.title: Fair Winds
popup.description: Rental Villa

popup.title: Marblehearth
popup.description: Rental Villa

popup.title: New Olamn
popup.description: The College of New Olamn, simply known as New Olamn, was a traditional bardic college

popup.title: Sahuagin Humbled
popup.description: The [[Walking Statue of Waterdeep]] known as the Sahuagin Humbled was originally the only Walking Statue visible in Waterdeep.

popup.title: Trollfort
popup.description: This structure stood four stories tall and was directly connected to the city walls that surrounded the Field Ward.

popup.title: The Red Gauntlet
popup.description: Food served here consisted mostly of dried fish, waybread, and rabbit-and-fowl stew. Drink consisted of a house wine. The fares were cheap in the Red Gauntlet with a plate of food running just 3 cp and a tankard 2 cp.

popup.title: Orm's Highbench
popup.description: Orm's Highbench was the headquarters of a trading company.

popup.title: Athal's Stables
popup.description: Athal's Stables were a stables. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles]], and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.title: T'Quession
popup.description: T'Quession was a [[sea elf]] hamlet.

popup.title: Turnstone Plumbing and Pipefitting
popup.description: Turnstone Plumbing and Pipefitting was a plumbing business that was owned by [[Jhalossan Turnstone]].

popup.title: The Redbridle Stables
popup.description: The Redbridle Stables were a stables that was owned by [[Rhazbos Redbridle]]. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles]], and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.title: Arnagus the Shipwright
popup.description: This was a large shipbuilding shed owned by [[Arnagus the Shipwright]].

popup.title: Thirsty Sailor
popup.description: The Thirsty Sailor was an infamous dive bar.

popup.title: Hlakken Stables
popup.description: The Hlakken Stables were a stables. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles,]] and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.title: The Jar
popup.description: The Jar was a small courtyard.

popup.title: Pampered Traveler
popup.description: Pampered Traveler was a fine establishment with large, well-furnished rooms, a play area for children, and a library that guests could peruse.

popup.title: Merchants' Rest
popup.description: Merchants' Rest, which was also known as the Coinscoffin, was a tomb. Despite its name, Merchants' Rest was reserved for anyone, whether they were a merchant or not, who prepaid to be interred within.

popup.title: Dunblast Roofing Company
popup.description: Dunblast Roofing Company was a carpentry business that was owned by [[Elemos Dunblast]] in the 14th century DR

popup.title: Mariners' Rest
popup.description: Mariners' Rest was a tomb. As its name implied, the tomb was reserved sailors and seamen who prepaid to be interred within.

popup.title: The Misty Beard
popup.description: Part of what made the Misty Beard famous up and down the [[Sword Coast]] was the staff which was composed of exotic or monstrous creatures from all over [[Faerûn]].

popup.title: Castle Waterdeep
popup.description: Castle Waterdeep was the seat of the city's government.

popup.title: The Golden Key Locksmiths
popup.description: The Golden Key Locksmiths, also known as The Golden Key, was a business owned by the locksmith [[Ansilver]] in the 14th century DR.

popup.title: Mud Flats
popup.description: The beach was frequented mostly by fishers, clam diggers, and occasional locals who enjoyed bathing in the cold waters of the [[Sea of Swords]].

popup.title: Sated Satyr
popup.description: The Sated Satyr was a two-story, irregularly shaped building that fronted the streets or the alley on all sides but one.

popup.title: Gerin's Breads
popup.description: Gerin's Breads was a bakery.

popup.title: Taurntyrith Adornments
popup.description: Taurntyrith dealed in door panels and wall panels of both painted and iridescent acid-treated copper and enamel. These predominantly depicted blue-green or blue-and-silver forest scenes.

popup.title: Khammeral's Coins
popup.description: Khammeral's Coins was a currency exchange.

popup.title: Rejviik's Mortuary
popup.description: Rejviik's Mortuary was a business.

popup.title: Deepwinter Vault
popup.description: The Deepwinter Vault was a mausoleum that belonged to the defunct noble [[Deepwinter (family) |Deepwinter]] family. It was also one of the entrances to the former lair of [[Artor Morlin]], the [[vampire lord]] of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Sultlue Vault
popup.description: The tomb was heavily warded with magic.

popup.title: Lords' Respite
popup.description: The Lords' Respite was reserved for any Lords of Waterdeep who wished to be buried there.

popup.title: Hlethvagi's Coins
popup.description: Hlethvagi's Coins was a moneychanging house.

popup.title: Tehmak's Coaches
popup.description: Tehma's Coaches provided coach and transportation services with the southern regions of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Amrani's Laundry
popup.description: Amrani's Laundry was a business owned by [[Amrani]].

popup.title: Tharqualnaar
popup.description: Tharqualnaar was a village of [[merfolk]] in Deepwater Harbor in Waterdeep, beneath Deepwater Isle.

popup.title: Amendsfarm
popup.description: A prison farm operated by the City Watch, where Waterdhavians convicted of minor offenses were sentenced to pay hard labor for a limited period of time.

popup.title: Mistshore
popup.description: Mistshore was the name given to the dilapidated north shore of Waterdeep's harbor in the late 15th century DR.[

popup.title: Southern Ward
popup.description: Southern Ward was the southeastern sector of the city of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Castle Ward
popup.description: The Castle Ward was the central ward of the city of Waterdeep.

popup.title: City of the Dead
popup.description: The City of the Dead was a large cemetery and ward in Waterdeep. Most of the city's dead were buried here. By day, it also doubled as the city's major public park picnic area.

popup.title: North Ward
popup.description: The North Ward was the northeastern sector of Waterdeep. It was famous for being the quietest ward of the city, consisting mostly of residential areas.

popup.title: Sea Ward
popup.description: The Sea Ward of Waterdeep was the wealthiest ward in Waterdeep and located in the northwest of the city.

popup.title: Seven Masks Theater
popup.description: The Seven Masks Theater was a theater that catered to the masses typically found in the neighborhood. Ship captains and sailors were admitted for free.

popup.title: Gull Leap
popup.description: A cliff along the northwestern edge of Waterdeep, just outside the Trollwall, that was named in part for the significant amount of [[sea gull]]s that nested upon it.
